title: An uncertainty principle for entanglement
abstract: Consider two orthonormal bases of a bipartite Hilbert space such that states in one basis are weakly entangled and states in the other are strongly entangled. We establish a quantitative version of the following uncertainty principle: every state that is localized in one basis must be delocalized in the other. More specifically, we lower bound the sum of the Shannon entropies of any state's coefficient distributions in the two bases by the difference between the entanglement Rényi entropies of their basis states. The result follows from new lower and upper bounds on the entanglement of superpositions that may be of independent interest. As an application, our result limits the power of weakly-entangled states in representing ground states of Hamiltonians with strongly-entangled energy eigenstates. We illustrate this application numerically for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model.
summary: This paper introduces a quantitative uncertainty principle for entanglement, bounding the sum of Shannon entropies in two different bases by the difference in entanglement Rényi entropies. This result has a direct physical implication, showing that weakly-entangled states cannot perfectly represent the ground states of systems whose energy eigenstates are highly entangled, demonstrated using the SYK model.
main_problem: The paper establishes a quantitative uncertainty principle for entanglement, generalizing known principles from position/momentum measurements.
main_result: It derives a lower bound on the sum of Shannon entropies of a state's coefficients in two orthonormal bases, relating it to the difference between the entanglement Rényi entropies of the basis states.
method: The proof relies on establishing new lower and upper bounds on the entanglement of superpositions, utilizing functional analysis tools like Schatten norms and interpolation theorems.
model_or_system: The primary application is to the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, which is used to illustrate how the uncertainty principle limits the ability of weakly-entangled states to represent ground states of Hamiltonians with strongly-entangled energy eigenstates.

why_interesting: It provides a fundamental mathematical constraint linking entanglement structure (basis localization) to energy structure (eigenbasis uncertainty), which is crucial for understanding quantum simulation and ground state preparation.
